stories.title: Cafe plan for empty Grade II listed shop on Holywell High Street
stories.summary: An empty shop in a Grade II listed building on Holywell High Street, once home to the Spread Eagle pub, could become a cafe under plans submitted to Flintshire Council. stories.title: Restaurant, flats and smaller Post Office planned for The Highway in Ewloe
stories.summary: Ewloe Post Office would be reduced in size to make room for a restaurant, with three flats created in the rest of the building, under plans submitted to Flintshire Council. stories.title: North Wales health board must find £17m more savings to secure £108m from Welsh Government
stories.summary: Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board is fighting to balance its books to secure £108 million of crucial extra central funding. Having already saved £46m this year however, if the board can make an additional £17m of savings – taking it’s annual savings to £63m – it will break even, retaining an £82m additional funding stream

stories.title: Penyffordd community garden paths resurfaced in £8,500 revamp
stories.summary: Potholed paths at a community garden in Penyffordd have been resurfaced and extended as part of an £8,500 revamp. The Millstone community garden and allotments have also gained raised beds, picnic benches and a commemorative tree. stories.title: Betsi Cadwaladr tops list of concerns raised with Healthcare Inspectorate Wales
stories.summary: North Wales’ health board had more concerns raised about it with the Welsh healthcare watchdog than any other NHS organisation in Wales in 2025-26. Healthcare Inspectorate Wales (HIW) received 115 concerns about Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board (BCUHB), ahead of 110 for Swansea Bay University Health Board, out of 783 in total.
